cards.claim: Critical batch size for Muon exists and is governed by momentum (β) and weight decay (λ)
cards.conditions: Four Muon variants (with/without Nesterov momentum and weight decay); nonconvex smooth loss; bounded gradient variance
cards.effect: The critical batch size formula predicts how hyperparameter changes scale the batch size that minimizes SFO complexity; variants differ only in how β and λ affect the ratio
cards.evidence: Theoretical lower bound (Proposition 4.3) with empirical validation across vision (FashionMNIST, ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, VGG16/CIFAR-100) and language modeling (Llama3.1 320M on C4)
cards.quote: We derive a lower bound on the critical batch size for the four Muon variants (Proposition 4.3). For example, for Muon with Nesterov momentum and weight decay we show [formula with β, λ, σ², ρ_max, ε] ...it identifies the qualitative scaling law: how the hyperparameters and govern , and how the ratio between variants depends only on and (the unknown quantities cancel). Our experiments validate these hyperparameter-dependent predictions

cards.claim: Larger momentum and batch size yield tighter convergence bounds; learning rate must scale down with larger momentum
cards.conditions: Muon without weight decay (Theorem 3.1) and with weight decay (Theorem 3.2); L-smooth nonconvex objective; bounded variance Assumption 2.2(ii)
cards.effect: Convergence rate upper bound improves (smaller) as β and B increase; enables larger batch sizes if momentum tuned correctly
cards.evidence: Convergence analysis via Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 with bound structure O(Lη + η²β/(1-β)² + √(ρ/(β·B)))
cards.quote: Theorem 3.1 suggests that setting the learning rate small and the momentum and batch size large results in a tighter bounds. For example, using [specific α and β] and [specific B] yields [rate].

cards.claim: Weight decay enforces almost-sure boundedness of parameter and gradient norms without assuming bounded gradients
cards.conditions: Muon with weight decay; requires learning rate condition λ < α/L²; assumptions 2.1 (L-smoothness) and 2.2 hold
cards.effect: Parameter norm and gradient norm remain bounded throughout training (Propositions 3.1, 3.2); enables implicit regularization without the common bounded-gradient assumption
cards.evidence: Theoretical results (Propositions 3.1 and 3.2) showing monotonic bound decrease with increasing λ until λ → ∞
cards.quote: Proposition 3.1 establishes that when [λ < α/L²], weight decay ensures the parameter norm remains almost surely bounded. Furthermore, the upper bound decreases monotonically with [λ], converging to [limit] as [λ → ∞].

cards.claim: Learning rate and weight decay must satisfy λ < α/L² for convergence guarantee with weight decay
cards.conditions: Muon with weight decay (Theorem 3.2); L-smooth loss; practically, this means λ ≪ α for typical He initialization (α ~ 10⁻³ and λ < 10⁻⁴)
cards.effect: Violation of this constraint can lead to divergence or poor convergence; typical practice (λ ≈ 10⁻⁵) easily satisfies this
cards.evidence: Theorem 3.2 convergence proof and Corollary 3.1; confirmed in experiments with α ∈ [10⁻⁴, 10⁻³], λ ∈ [10⁻⁵, 10⁻⁴] (see Figure 1)
cards.quote: Theorem 3.2 (i) and (ii) ... requires that the weight decay coefficient satisfy [λ < α/L²], which recommends using a small [λ]. In practice, [λ] is often used with values much smaller than 1, and this assumption can also be considered realistic. For practical reference, under He initialization...the condition is satisfied for all weight decay values used in our experiments ([λ] ≤ 10⁻⁴).

cards.claim: Effective rank of gradient matrices is much smaller than full dimension; variance scales with rank not dimension
cards.conditions: Deep neural networks in over-parameterized regimes; FashionMNIST MLP example shows ρ = 32 vs d = 100; LLM evidence: rank-fraction 0.05 suffices for models up to 3B parameters
cards.effect: Muon's convergence bound (with variance term ~√(ρ/(β·B))) can be substantially tighter than vector-based methods (with variance ~√(d/(β·B))): factor of 3.1× in FashionMNIST example
cards.evidence: Empirical measurement (Appendix I) and citation of Ahn et al. (2025); theoretical comparison with SGD bound structure
cards.quote: To make this comparison concrete, Appendix I measures [ρ] directly on a controlled FashionMNIST MLP and finds [ρ_max] = 32 for the layer, compared to d = 100. Since the SGD-type variance term scales with d while the Muon bound scales with ρ, this translates to a variance-term reduction factor of [3.1×]

cards.claim: Batch-size scaling laws depend on gradient variance and effective rank; CBS scales inversely with variance and rank
cards.conditions: SFO complexity minimization framework; nonconvex smooth loss; CBS formula contains σ² (gradient variance) and ρ_max (rank) as unknowns
cards.effect: Doubling batch size (1024→2048) requires rank and variance to not increase proportionally to maintain same critical batch size; if variance or rank grows with batch size, CBS shifts upward
cards.evidence: Proposition 4.3 lower bound formula and Section 4 analysis; validated on multiple workloads (FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10/100, C4/Llama3.1)
cards.quote: Our theoretical analysis characterizes the critical batch size as a function of the gradient variance and optimization hyperparameters. While explicitly modeling the dependence of [B_CBS] on model width or depth is beyond the scope of this single-matrix analysis, our results establish the fundamental relationship [B_CBS ~ σ²/(rank-dependent terms)]. This suggests that scaling behaviors observed in larger models are mediated through changes in their gradient noise properties.

cards.claim: Newton-Schulz approximation error is negligible in practice; SVD vs. N-S performance gap ≤ 0.15 percentage points
cards.conditions: Muon with finite Newton-Schulz iterations (k fixed in practice); convergence bound differs by O(2^{-2k}) decay term
cards.effect: Using practical Newton-Schulz (~20 iterations) incurs negligible cost vs. exact SVD; validates using Newton-Schulz approximation in all experiments
cards.evidence: Proposition 3.3 theoretical bound and Table 8 (Appendix); empirical comparison across four network widths
cards.quote: Our own experiments comparing [exact SVD and Newton-Schulz iterations] across four network widths (Appendix, Table 8) also show that while [exact SVD] reduces the approximation error, the test accuracy gain is at most [0.15] percentage points, confirming that the gap is negligible in practice.

cards.claim: Nesterov momentum provides modest convergence improvement; bounds are similar with or without Nesterov
cards.conditions: Muon with/without Nesterov across four variants (Theorems 3.1, 3.2); L-smooth nonconvex loss
cards.effect: Bounds slightly tighter with Nesterov (some terms in upper bound smaller); practical difference not substantial but consistent
cards.evidence: Theorem 3.1(i) vs 3.1(ii) and Theorem 3.2(i) vs 3.2(ii) comparison; Nesterov terms only affect initialization-dependent O(d/η) term negligibly for large iterations
cards.quote: Theorem 3.1 shows that Muon, both with and without Nesterov momentum, converges to a neighborhood of a stationary point, and achieves same upper bounds on convergence. Note that some terms in the upper bound are slightly smaller when Nesterov momentum is used.

cards.claim: Muon respects matrix structure and provides structure-aware convergence guarantee via nuclear norm, not Frobenius norm
cards.conditions: Muon's analysis uses nuclear norm (rank-dependent) vs. SGD's Euclidean/Frobenius norm; matrix parameters in DNNs
cards.effect: Convergence criteria are stricter but more aligned with intrinsic structure; potentially explains empirical advantage over SGD/AdamW
cards.evidence: Theoretical comparison in Section 3.1; nuclear norm is stronger criterion than Frobenius norm
cards.quote: Since [nuclear norm ≥ Frobenius norm], a convergence guarantee in terms of the nuclear norm is stronger than that in terms of the Frobenius norm. Therefore, compared to conventional methods such as SGD with momentum, which effectively ignore the matrix structure through vectorization, Muon respects the matrix structure and is shown to converge under a stricter analytical criterion given by the nuclear norm.
